response.reason:
Six numbered NL segments describe: (1) a simple state for human driving mode, (2) a composite/sub-machine state for autonomous mode, (3) power-on transition into human driving mode (also implying root initial entry), (4) autonomous entry condition based on front_distance, (4.2) autonomous exit condition(s) back to human driving mode with multiple alternatives (event, guard, and containment-scoped condition 'in (auto final)'), and (5) power-off transition to a final state. Contracts were split by independently violable property: element_declaration for the two named states, initial_entry for power-on establishing root/system start into human driving mode, transition_endpoints for human->autonomous, autonomous->human, and termination for power-off to final state. Guard/trigger details are preserved in transition_groups per alternative (now with required reason/basis fields at the group level). No guard_disjointness contract was added since NL4.2 lists AND-ed conditions on a single transition, not distinguishable alternatives requiring mutual exclusion. No state_action contracts were manufactured since no continuous/repeated activity is stated. No cardinality contract emitted for NL2's "sub-states" because no explicit count or named list is given.</reason>

arguments.reason: This lens audits contract completeness and structural consistency across author source (PlantUML/canonical IR) and closed FCSTM. Key findings: (1) NL3 requires root/system power-on entry into HumanDrivingMode; the closed model has a proper root->HumanDriving edge triggered by Power_On (transition:line:20 wait, actually two initial edges exist: [*]->HumanDriving with /Power_On at line 20 in text mapping to transition:line:20 per inspection facts, which is flagged INITIAL_ENTRY_CONDITIONAL/unreachable because it carries a trigger). The exact owner-local root initial edge to HumanDriving is conditioned on an event trigger rather than being the required unconditional default entry, and is marked reachable_from_initial=false and its declared event Power_On has no reachable consumer. This is a genuine initial_entry defect on the exact contract-required owner (root) edge to HumanDriving. (2) NL2-DERIVED containment of AutonomousMode sub-states is satisfied (Navigating, Parking direct children) - omit. (3) NL4 endpoint HumanDriving->AutonomousMode exists (transition:line:21) with correct semantic effect, but its guard is empty although NL4-DERIVED requires exact guard front_distance>10; the transition trigger is event front_distance_10 with no guard field, so guard content is missing -- but this is really an event vs guard modeling question already covered by NL4-DERIVED contract; that's assessed by other lens likely (behavior_consequence). I will focus on structural aspects: transition_endpoints existence, guard presence/absence for NL4-DERIVED contract, trigger_set correctness for NL4.2-DERIVED, and guard presence for NL4.2-DERIVED. (4) NL4.2 endpoint AutonomousMode->HumanDrivingMode: composite-to-composite transition exists (transition:line:19, Autonomous->HumanDriving) guarded by R45RouteToken==6, with no explicit trigger event (triggers=[]); NL4.2-DERIVED trigger_set requires exact event 'receive human steering cmd' but transition:line:19 has no trigger at all (triggers=[]), while the actual named event 'Human_Steering_Cmd_Brake_Pressed' only appears on inner region transitions (line:16,17) that exit the region via [*] and set the route token, not on the composite-level transition itself. This is a structural mismatch: the composite-to-HumanDriving transition (which is the one satisfying NL4.2-ENDPOINT-1) carries guard R45RouteToken==6 but no trigger, so the required trigger_set is missing on the actual carrier transition. (5) NL5 termination: HumanDriving->[*] final exists (transition:line:22) triggered by Power_Off - this appears structurally fine as an outer scope transition to final. NL5-ENDPOINT-1 requires System->FinalState; carrier exists as HumanDriving->[*] but NL5 states 'the system' should transition when power off - HumanDriving is the exact operating scope at time of power-off per source, so this seems satisfied structurally. I omit it here since no structural inconsistency found beyond what behavior lens may check re: re-entry.

arguments.reason: This lens audits contract completeness and structural consistency across author source (PlantUML/canonical IR) and closed FCSTM. Key findings: (1) NL3 requires root/system power-on entry into HumanDrivingMode; the closed model's owner-local initial edge (transition:line:20, [*] -> HumanDriving : /Power_On) is flagged by inspection_equivalent_facts as reachable_from_initial=false with diagnostic INITIAL_ENTRY_CONDITIONAL and EVENT_CONSUMER_UNREACHABLE, and verify_facts marks the corresponding check as refuted. This is a genuine structural initial-entry defect on the exact contract-required owner (root) edge to HumanDriving, distinct from mere existence. (2) NL2-DERIVED containment of AutonomousMode sub-states (Navigating, Parking) is satisfied - omitted. (3) NL4 endpoint HumanDriving->AutonomousMode exists (transition:line:21) - satisfied structurally, omitted; its guard-content gap is a distinct property assessed elsewhere. (4) NL4.2 endpoint AutonomousMode->HumanDrivingMode is realized by transition:line:19 (Autonomous->HumanDriving, guard R45RouteToken==6) - endpoint itself satisfied, omitted from candidates. However the exact carrier transition for this endpoint has triggers=[] (no event), while NL4.2-DERIVED requires the trigger 'receive human steering cmd'; the actual Human_Steering_Cmd_Brake_Pressed event is declared only on inner region-exit transitions (line:16/17) targeting the region-local final pseudostate, not on the composite-level carrier. This is a structural trigger_set mismatch on the exact bound carrier. (5) NL5 termination via HumanDriving->[*] (transition:line:22, Power_Off) appears structurally fine as an outer-scope transition to final; no structural inconsistency found here for this lens (re-entry/termination stability is left to the behavior-consequence lens).

The exact deterministic facts show (1) the root/system power-on initial edge (transition:line:20, source [*], target HumanDriving) carries a Power_On trigger and is refuted as an initial_entry check and marked reachable_from_initial=false, while the event_consumer fact for Power_On shows zero reachable consumer transitions/states; (2) the AutonomousMode->HumanDrivingMode transition (transition:line:19) is a satisfied endpoint/trigger-adjacent fact but the trigger set is empty (no Human_Steering_Cmd_Brake_Pressed trigger on that carrier; that event is instead consumed only by the two Navigating/Parking->[*] segments), so the NL4.2 trigger_set contract is mismatched at its actual carrier; (3) the FinalState termination target for HumanDriving->[*] (transition:line:22) is a bare final pseudostate with no re-entry, so termination itself looks stable, but the true root-level power-on entry is conditional/refuted, which is the dominant behavioral defect chain feeding NL3's initial_entry contract. I preserve NL3 as the primary initial_entry candidate (S2-ineligible since the edge exists but is conditional/guarded by an unresolved trigger-only pseudostate semantics per INITIAL_ENTRY_CONDITIONAL diagnostic), and add one derived event_consumer_coverage contract for Power_On because the declared consumer transition never reaches a consumer state from top-level initial entry, matching the explicit EVENT_CONSUMER_UNREACHABLE diagnostic and refuted verify_facts check. I do not fold this into NL3 because event-consumer coverage and initial-entry are independent frontier properties per the routing discipline. NL4.2's trigger contract is evaluated against the exact carrier transition:line:19, whose triggers list is empty, showing a mismatch between the required 'receive human steering cmd' trigger and the actual empty trigger set on the bound transition. NL5 termination and NL5 endpoint are satisfied (HumanDriving->[*] exists, target is a bare final state, no re-entry), so they are omitted. NL1, NL2, NL2-DERIVED containment, NL4-ENDPOINT, NL4-DERIVED guard, and NL4.2-ENDPOINT are satisfied structurally per the exact inventories and are omitted from this lens per sparse-response rules (structural satisfaction is primarily the contract_structure_contrast lens's concern, but I confirm no behavioral defect attaches to them).

candidates.basis: inspection_equivalent_facts.transitions[line:20] (trigger=Power_On, reachable_from_initial=false); inspection_equivalent_facts.diagnostics[INITIAL_ENTRY_CONDITIONAL]; verify_facts.checks.non_proved[initial-entry:transition:line:20]=refuted; reference_inspection_facts.diagnostics[W_INITIAL_UNCONDITIONAL_MISSING].
candidates.expected: On power-on the root/system must unconditionally enter HumanDrivingMode via the required initial pseudostate edge, matching the exact owner (root '[*]') and target (HumanDriving) hints.
candidates.observed: The only owner-local edge realizing this obligation is transition:line:20 ([*] -> HumanDriving), but it carries trigger Power_On and reachable_from_initial=false; verify_facts marks check_id=initial-entry:transition:line:20 as status=refuted (has_trigger=true, has_guard=false); reference_inspection_facts diagnostic W_INITIAL_UNCONDITIONAL_MISSING explicitly flags the missing unconditional fallback entry for this exact composite_path, and inspection_equivalent_facts diagnostic INITIAL_ENTRY_CONDITIONAL confirms the initial pseudostate transition carries a trigger.
candidates.reason: The exact owner-local root initial edge required by NL3 exists structurally but is conditional (carries a trigger) and is deterministically marked unreachable from initial and refuted by the owned verify_facts initial-entry check, which is a direct behavioral-consequence defect on the exact contract's owner/target obligation.
candidates.requirement_quote: when power on, the system turn into human driving mode
candidates.strongest_rebuttal: The edge does target the exact required state (HumanDriving) and is the only structural initial edge at root scope, so a reviewer could argue endpoint identity alone satisfies a loose reading of 'must_enter'; however the explicit refuted verify_facts check and unreachable-from-initial flag show the edge does not realize unconditional default entry, which is what 'when power on, the system turn into human driving mode' requires as an unqualified startup obligation.

candidates.basis: inspection_equivalent_facts.event_consumers[event=Power_On] (declared vs reachable sets); inspection_equivalent_facts.diagnostics[EVENT_CONSUMER_UNREACHABLE]; verify_facts.checks.non_proved[event-consumer:Power_On]=refuted.

candidates.reason: This is a derived causal property: NL3 establishes Power_On as the exact required startup event, and cross-view grounding reveals the event's declared consumer is not reachable, which the NL-only contract extraction (initial_entry only) does not directly state as a consumer-coverage obligation. No frozen predicate exactly expresses event-consumer reachability, so predicate_id is null and this remains a precise W1 candidate rather than being silently dropped.

candidates.basis: inspection_equivalent_facts.transitions[line:19] triggers=[]; inspection_equivalent_facts.event_consumers[event=Human_Steering_Cmd_Brake_Pressed] consumer_transition_refs=[transition:line:16,transition:line:17]; fcstm_model.text (Autonomous -> HumanDriving guarded only by R45RouteToken==6, no trigger).
candidates.expected: The transition from AutonomousMode to HumanDrivingMode must be triggered by the exact event 'receive human steering cmd' (Human_Steering_Cmd_Brake_Pressed).

candidates.reason: The trigger_set contract requires the exact event 'receive human steering cmd' on the AutonomousMode->HumanDrivingMode transition; the exact bound carrier's parsed trigger list is empty, which is a precise S3 mismatch even though the same net behavior may be achieved through an internal macro chain.
candidates.requirement_quote: transit to human driving mode when receive human steering cmd, brake pressed, in (auto final)
candidates.strongest_rebuttal: A defender could argue the macro/compiler-owned decomposition (internal exit segments setting R45RouteToken=6, then the outer transition guarded by R45RouteToken==6) collectively realizes the same NL4.2 obligation end-to-end, so the trigger is present in the macro's internal segment rather than absent; however per the transition-endpoints/trigger_set property, the exact carrier bound to the AutonomousMode->HumanDrivingMode relation (transition:line:19) itself has an empty trigger set, so the specific trigger_set contract on that exact carrier is not satisfied even if the macro-composed guard achieves the same net effect.

result.reason: This lens audits behavioral consequences: root-level initial entry, event-consumer reachability, and termination stability across the closed FCSTM for pair 0030. The exact deterministic facts show (1) the root/system power-on initial edge (transition:line:20, source [*], target HumanDriving) carries a Power_On trigger and is refuted as an initial_entry check and marked reachable_from_initial=false, while the event_consumer fact for Power_On shows zero reachable consumer transitions/states; (2) the AutonomousMode->HumanDrivingMode transition (transition:line:19) is a satisfied endpoint/trigger-adjacent fact but the trigger set is empty (no Human_Steering_Cmd_Brake_Pressed trigger on that carrier; that event is instead consumed only by the two Navigating/Parking->[*] segments), so the NL4.2 trigger_set contract is mismatched at its actual carrier; (3) the FinalState termination target for HumanDriving->[*] (transition:line:22) is a bare final pseudostate with no re-entry, so termination itself looks stable, but the true root-level power-on entry is conditional/refuted, which is the dominant behavioral defect chain feeding NL3's initial_entry contract. I preserve NL3 as the primary initial_entry candidate (S2-ineligible since the edge exists but is conditional/guarded by an unresolved trigger-only pseudostate semantics per INITIAL_ENTRY_CONDITIONAL diagnostic), and add one derived event_consumer_coverage contract for Power_On because the declared consumer transition never reaches a consumer state from top-level initial entry, matching the explicit EVENT_CONSUMER_UNREACHABLE diagnostic and refuted verify_facts check. I do not fold this into NL3 because event-consumer coverage and initial-entry are independent frontier properties per the routing discipline. NL4.2's trigger contract is evaluated against the exact carrier transition:line:19, whose triggers list is empty, showing a mismatch between the required 'receive human steering cmd' trigger and the actual empty trigger set on the bound transition. NL5 termination and NL5 endpoint are satisfied (HumanDriving->[*] exists, target is a bare final state, no re-entry), so they are omitted. NL1, NL2, NL2-DERIVED containment, NL4-ENDPOINT, NL4-DERIVED guard, and NL4.2-ENDPOINT are satisfied structurally per the exact inventories and are omitted from this lens per sparse-response rules (structural satisfaction is primarily the contract_structure_contrast lens's concern, but I confirm no behavioral defect attaches to them).

issues.strongest_rebuttal: The edge does target the exact required state (HumanDriving) and is the only structural initial edge at root scope, so a reviewer could argue endpoint identity alone satisfies a loose reading of 'must_enter'; however the explicit refuted verify_facts check and unreachable-from-initial flag show the edge does not realize unconditional default entry, which is what 'when power on, the system turn into human driving mode' requires as an unqualified startup obligation.
issues.title: Root power-on initial entry to HumanDriving is conditional/refuted, not an unconditional default edge

issues.expected: The power-on stimulus that is required to drive the system into HumanDrivingMode must have at least one operationally reachable consumer transition/state from the top-level initial entry, since NL3 establishes power-on as the triggering event for the required startup obligation.
issues.observed: inspection_equivalent_facts.event_consumers for event Power_On lists consumer_transition_refs=[transition:line:20] but reachable_consumer_state_refs=[] and reachable_consumer_transition_refs=[]; the diagnostic EVENT_CONSUMER_UNREACHABLE explicitly states 'Event Power_On has consumers but none is reachable from a top-level initial entry'; verify_facts confirms check_id=event-consumer:Power_On is refuted.
issues.reason: This is a derived causal property: NL3 establishes Power_On as the exact required startup event, and cross-view grounding reveals the event's declared consumer is not reachable, which the NL-only contract extraction (initial_entry only) does not directly state as a consumer-coverage obligation. No frozen predicate exactly expresses event-consumer reachability, so predicate_id is null and this remains a precise W1 candidate rather than being silently dropped.
issues.requirement_quote: when power on, the system turn into human driving mode
issues.strongest_rebuttal: One could argue Power_On's sole purpose is exactly the initial-entry edge already captured by NL3, so this is the same defect restated under a different property; however event-consumer coverage and initial-entry are tracked as independent frontier properties per protocol, and the consumer-reachability fact (zero reachable consumer refs) is a distinct deterministic signal from the initial-entry refutation, so both must be preserved as separate exact obligations rather than merged into one.
issues.title: Power_On event has a declared consumer transition but zero reachable consumer states/transitions from root initial entry

issues.basis: inspection_equivalent_facts.transitions[line:19] triggers=[]; inspection_equivalent_facts.event_consumers[event=Human_Steering_Cmd_Brake_Pressed] consumer_transition_refs=[transition:line:16,transition:line:17]; fcstm_model.text (Autonomous -> HumanDriving guarded only by R45RouteToken==6, no trigger).
issues.expected: The transition from AutonomousMode to HumanDrivingMode must be triggered by the exact event 'receive human steering cmd' (Human_Steering_Cmd_Brake_Pressed).
issues.observed: The exact bound carrier transition:line:19 (Autonomous -> HumanDriving) has triggers=[] and guard='R45RouteToken == 6'; the Human_Steering_Cmd_Brake_Pressed event is instead declared and reachably consumed only by transition:line:16 (Navigating -> [*]) and transition:line:17 (Parking -> [*]), which are internal region-exit segments feeding a compiler-owned route token rather than the outer Autonomous->HumanDriving transition itself.
issues.reason: The trigger_set contract requires the exact event 'receive human steering cmd' on the AutonomousMode->HumanDrivingMode transition; the exact bound carrier's parsed trigger list is empty, which is a precise S3 mismatch even though the same net behavior may be achieved through an internal macro chain.
issues.requirement_quote: transit to human driving mode when receive human steering cmd, brake pressed, in (auto final)
issues.strongest_rebuttal: A defender could argue the macro/compiler-owned decomposition (internal exit segments setting R45RouteToken=6, then the outer transition guarded by R45RouteToken==6) collectively realizes the same NL4.2 obligation end-to-end, so the trigger is present in the macro's internal segment rather than absent; however per the transition-endpoints/trigger_set property, the exact carrier bound to the AutonomousMode->HumanDrivingMode relation (transition:line:19) itself has an empty trigger set, so the specific trigger_set contract on that exact carrier is not satisfied even if the macro-composed guard achieves the same net effect.
issues.title: AutonomousMode->HumanDrivingMode transition carries no trigger; required event is consumed only by internal Navigating/Parking exit segments

Contracts were split by independently violable property: element_declaration for the two named states, initial_entry for power-on establishing root/system start into human driving mode, transition_endpoints for human->autonomous, autonomous->human, and termination for power-off to final state. Guard/trigger details are preserved in transition_groups per alternative (now with required reason/basis fields at the group level). No guard_disjointness contract was added since NL4.2 lists AND-ed conditions on a single transition, not distinguishable alternatives requiring mutual exclusion. No state_action contracts were manufactured since no continuous/repeated activity is stated. No cardinality contract emitted for NL2's "sub-states" because no explicit count or named list is given.</reason>

branches.reason: This lens audits behavioral consequences: root-level initial entry, event-consumer reachability, and termination stability across the closed FCSTM for pair 0030. The exact deterministic facts show (1) the root/system power-on initial edge (transition:line:20, source [*], target HumanDriving) carries a Power_On trigger and is refuted as an initial_entry check and marked reachable_from_initial=false, while the event_consumer fact for Power_On shows zero reachable consumer transitions/states; (2) the AutonomousMode->HumanDrivingMode transition (transition:line:19) is a satisfied endpoint/trigger-adjacent fact but the trigger set is empty (no Human_Steering_Cmd_Brake_Pressed trigger on that carrier; that event is instead consumed only by the two Navigating/Parking->[*] segments), so the NL4.2 trigger_set contract is mismatched at its actual carrier; (3) the FinalState termination target for HumanDriving->[*] (transition:line:22) is a bare final pseudostate with no re-entry, so termination itself looks stable, but the true root-level power-on entry is conditional/refuted, which is the dominant behavioral defect chain feeding NL3's initial_entry contract. I preserve NL3 as the primary initial_entry candidate (S2-ineligible since the edge exists but is conditional/guarded by an unresolved trigger-only pseudostate semantics per INITIAL_ENTRY_CONDITIONAL diagnostic), and add one derived event_consumer_coverage contract for Power_On because the declared consumer transition never reaches a consumer state from top-level initial entry, matching the explicit EVENT_CONSUMER_UNREACHABLE diagnostic and refuted verify_facts check. I do not fold this into NL3 because event-consumer coverage and initial-entry are independent frontier properties per the routing discipline. NL4.2's trigger contract is evaluated against the exact carrier transition:line:19, whose triggers list is empty, showing a mismatch between the required 'receive human steering cmd' trigger and the actual empty trigger set on the bound transition. NL5 termination and NL5 endpoint are satisfied (HumanDriving->[*] exists, target is a bare final state, no re-entry), so they are omitted. NL1, NL2, NL2-DERIVED containment, NL4-ENDPOINT, NL4-DERIVED guard, and NL4.2-ENDPOINT are satisfied structurally per the exact inventories and are omitted from this lens per sparse-response rules (structural satisfaction is primarily the contract_structure_contrast lens's concern, but I confirm no behavioral defect attaches to them).

stage_receipts.reason:
Six numbered NL segments describe: (1) a simple state for human driving mode, (2) a composite/sub-machine state for autonomous mode, (3) power-on transition into human driving mode (also implying root initial entry), (4) autonomous entry condition based on front_distance, (4.2) autonomous exit condition(s) back to human driving mode with multiple alternatives (event, guard, and containment-scoped condition 'in (auto final)'), and (5) power-off transition to a final state. Contracts were split by independently violable property: element_declaration for the two named states, initial_entry for power-on establishing root/system start into human driving mode, transition_endpoints for human->autonomous, autonomous->human, and termination for power-off to final state. Guard/trigger details are preserved in transition_groups per alternative (now with required reason/basis fields at the group level). No guard_disjointness contract was added since NL4.2 lists AND-ed conditions on a single transition, not distinguishable alternatives requiring mutual exclusion. No state_action contracts were manufactured since no continuous/repeated activity is stated. No cardinality contract emitted for NL2's "sub-states" because no explicit count or named list is given.</reason>
